lead: Network access control (NAC) decides whether a device may join a network and what it may reach. It exists because a wall socket or Wi-Fi signal is not proof of trust: any laptop can plug in. IEEE 802.1X carries authentication before the switch forwards ordinary traffic. EAP is the flexible authentication conversation; RADIUS carries it to a central server. A VPN (virtual private network) extends a private network over the Internet using authentication and a tunnel. Offices use NAC at the edge; remote workers use VPNs daily.
prereq: You need: 802.1X in wireless networks, IPsec, TLS, and certificates from Unit 4.

blocks.text: 802.1X is port-based access control. It has three roles. The supplicant is software on the client that proves identity. The authenticator is the switch or access point that controls the port. The authentication server is a RADIUS server (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) that checks credentials and policy. The switch does not store every user password; it relays.

An Ethernet switch port starts unauthorized. In this state it forwards only EAPOL frames. EAPOL means EAP over LAN; EAP is the Extensible Authentication Protocol, a framework for request and response messages, not one fixed method. Normal IP packets are dropped.

items: Link comes up; the supplicant sends EAPOL-Start.
The supplicant replies with an identity, for example alice.
The switch puts the EAP message inside a RADIUS Access-Request to the server.
Server and supplicant run an EAP method; the switch passes messages between them.

The server sends Access-Accept or Access-Reject. Accept may include Tunnel-Private-Group-ID, a RADIUS attribute carrying a VLAN identifier. A VLAN is a virtual LAN, an isolated Layer 2 broadcast domain.
The switch moves the port to authorized and places it in that VLAN. Access-Reject leaves it unauthorized.

blocks.text: EAP methods differ in how they protect credentials. EAP-TLS uses certificates on both supplicant and server; it gives mutual authentication and needs client-certificate management. PEAP (Protected EAP) uses a server certificate only; a TLS tunnel protects an inner authentication, often a password method. EAP-TTLS (Tunneled TLS) is similar and can carry legacy inner methods. EAP alone has no encryption; PEAP and EAP-TTLS wrap the inner exchange in TLS, while EAP-TLS uses TLS with certificates on both sides. See TLS.

NAC is the policy layer around 802.1X. It asks not only who you are but whether the device is healthy. A posture check inspects OS patch level, antivirus status, disk encryption, or mandatory software. A failed check can put the device in a quarantine VLAN with only a remediation server. After remediation, the device can reauthenticate. RADIUS Change of Authorization can move a live session.
Posture assessment details are advanced; only a few universities teach them. The exam level is: identity plus device state plus VLAN decision.

sections.h3: VPNs: remote access, site-to-site and tunneling

blocks.text: A VPN builds a protected tunnel over the Internet. It gives confidentiality, integrity and authentication for traffic between endpoints.

items: Remote access VPN: one user device connects to a VPN gateway. Used for work from home. Often TLS-based or IPsec.
Site-to-site VPN: two gateways, for example a Chennai office and a Mumbai office, connect networks. End hosts do not run VPN software.
IPsec VPN: network-layer protection for all IP traffic in the tunnel; see IPsec. Good for site-to-site.
SSL/TLS VPN: uses TLS; often browser-based access to a few apps, or a client tunnel. The name says SSL, but modern versions use TLS.

blocks.text: Split tunneling decides routing. With split tunneling, only traffic for private subnets goes through the tunnel; Internet traffic goes direct. It saves gateway bandwidth, but the device is on two networks at once, so malware can bridge between them. Full tunneling sends all traffic through the gateway, giving central filtering.
MFA (multi-factor authentication) combines factors; see user authentication. A VPN should require MFA before it creates the tunnel, because a stolen password alone must not open the office network.

spec.aria: Sequence diagram between alice, the switch port Fa0/10 and the RADIUS server: EAPOL-Start, identity request and response, Access-Request, the relayed EAP method, Access-Accept with group ID 20, EAP-Success. The port bar turns from unauthorized to authorized, and two boxes give 0 VLANs before and VLAN 20 after.

examples.question: User alice connects to switch port Fa0/10. Before authentication the port is unauthorized. RADIUS returns Access-Accept with Tunnel-Private-Group-ID = 20. What changes? State the VLAN and the number of normal-traffic VLANs allowed on that port before authentication.
steps: Before authentication, port Fa0/10 is unauthorized. It accepts EAPOL frames only; normal data frames are dropped.
Alice's supplicant sends EAPOL-Start. The switch asks for identity. Alice sends alice.
The switch sends RADIUS Access-Request to the server. The server authenticates alice and returns Access-Accept with Tunnel-Private-Group-ID = 20.
The switch reads the attribute value 20. It marks the port authorized and assigns VLAN 20.
Normal traffic from alice now enters VLAN 20. Before step 4, normal traffic used 0 VLANs on that port.
examples.answer: The port becomes authorized and carries VLAN 20 traffic; before authentication, normal traffic on that port belongs to zero VLANs because only EAPOL is allowed.

traps: The switch is the authenticator, not the authentication server. The RADIUS server makes the accept or reject decision.
EAP alone has no encryption. PEAP and EAP-TTLS protect the inner method with TLS; EAP-TLS uses certificates on both sides.
An unauthorized 802.1X port is not dead: it still passes EAPOL frames. Saying the port is down loses marks.
IPsec VPN works at the network layer; an SSL/TLS VPN uses TLS. A browser-based SSL VPN does not protect every IP packet by itself.
Split tunneling is a routing choice, not an encryption method. It can reduce load but widens the device's exposure.

quiz.q: Name the three 802.1X roles and say which device is the authenticator.
quiz.a: Supplicant, authenticator, authentication server. The switch or access point is the authenticator.

quiz.q: Why is EAP called a framework rather than a single authentication method?
quiz.a: EAP defines request and response messages that carry many methods, such as EAP-TLS, PEAP and EAP-TTLS. The method is chosen inside the EAP conversation.

quiz.q: RADIUS returns Access-Reject for alice. What is the port state and what traffic can pass?
quiz.a: The port stays unauthorized. Only EAPOL frames can pass; normal data traffic is dropped.

quiz.q: Compare EAP-TLS and PEAP on certificate needs and trust.
quiz.a: EAP-TLS needs a client certificate and a server certificate, so both sides authenticate with certificates. PEAP needs only a server certificate; the client validates the server certificate and protects an inner password method inside TLS.

quiz.q: What does a RADIUS Tunnel-Private-Group-ID attribute tell a switch?
quiz.a: It gives the VLAN identifier that the switch should assign to the authorized port for that session, for example VLAN 20.

quiz.q: Give one benefit and one risk of split tunneling.
quiz.a: Benefit: only private-subnet traffic uses the VPN gateway, saving bandwidth. Risk: the device is on the private network and the Internet at the same time, so malware can bridge and expose the private network.

quiz.q: What does a posture check test in NAC?
quiz.a: It tests device health, such as OS patch level, antivirus status, disk encryption, or required software, before granting normal access.

quiz.q: A company wants a browser-based VPN for contractors to reach one web app. Which VPN type fits and why?
quiz.a: An SSL/TLS VPN fits. It uses TLS in the browser, needs no full IPsec client, and can limit contractors to the selected web application.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern offices combine 802.1X with device certificates and endpoint detection, not just user passwords. Cloud zero-trust designs replace the idea of a trusted inside network with per-application checks. VPNs are being supplemented by ZTNA (Zero Trust Network Access), which grants access to one application rather than a whole subnet. Search next for 802.1X EAP-TLS deployment, RADIUS Change of Authorization, ZTNA versus VPN, and posture assessment.
